sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Clayton County?
sections.html:
Two separate Clayton County offices touch every parcel. Value comes from the Board of Tax Assessors. The bill, the collection and the split of the money among the county, the cities, fire services and the school board come from the Tax Commissioner. Neither office picks the millage rate: the Board of Commissioners picks the county's, and the other taxing bodies pick theirs.

You will find both under one roof in the Jonesboro government complex on South McDonough Street (number 121). The assessors are on the fourth floor of Annex 3, phone (770) 477-3285. The Tax Commissioner is on the second floor of the same annex, and the property tax line is (770) 477-3311. Knowing which door to knock on saves a seller days, because a value question sent to the commissioner or a payoff question sent to the assessors simply gets redirected.

Value is fixed as of January 1. A house sold in October still shows up on the bill under whoever held it on that January date, so the bill and the closing statement have to be read side by side.

sections.h2: What is Clayton County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Clayton County is a compact, heavily built-up county south of Atlanta. At 144 square miles, only two Georgia counties are smaller. Jonesboro holds the courthouse, Forest Park is the biggest city, and Clayton State University is in Morrow. The county also holds most of Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport.

The 2020 census counted 297,595 residents, 106,200 households and 114,038 housing units, with 6.9% of those units vacant. Renters edged out owners in 2020, at 50.5% of occupied homes to 49.5%, and the median age was 34.3. A landlord selling with tenants in place is a common situation here, and the lease is one more item to settle before a closing date.

The county sits across two river basins, with the eastern side between Forest Park and Lovejoy draining toward the Ocmulgee and the western side toward the Flint. Interstates 75, 85, 285 and 675 all cross it, along with US 19/41 (Tara Boulevard) and State Routes 54, 85 and 138. Conley and Irondale are census-designated places, and Ellenwood, Rex and Mountain View are unincorporated communities. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether your parcel also carries a city bill.

sections.h2: When are Clayton County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner's own presentation describes a yearly rhythm. Assessment notices go out in spring or early summer, the millage rate process runs from about mid July to mid August, and bills follow around mid September, with a due date usually in mid November. The presentation puts the payment window at 60 days after mail-out. Those dates shift each year, and the printed bill and the office line, (770) 477-3311, give the real ones.

If your value is under appeal when bills go out, you receive two bills. One covers 85% and falls due with everyone else's. The other covers the remaining 15% and comes due, or comes back as a refund, after the appeal settles. Request a copy of both before you list the house.

The state revenue department's county fact sheet adds two statewide rules. Interest waits until 60 days after the bill's postmark, though penalties can follow on delinquent balances. A claim for tax assessed in error has to begin within three years of payment, and appeal refunds are issued once the final value is set.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Clayton County property assessment?
sections.html:
The clock is 45 days, counted from the mailing date shown on the notice, and the appeal has to be written. Homestead applications and other specialized assessment requests ride on that same date. A late filing forfeits that year's challenge. File with the assessors in Annex 3, or through the county's online appeals site.

After the first review, the notice names four routes.

Appeal routes listed on the Clayton County notice of assessment (Clayton County Board of Tax Assessors)
RouteWhat it can decideCondition printed on the notice
Board of EqualizationValue, uniformity, exemptions or taxabilityOpen to any owner who files in time
Nonbinding arbitrationValue onlyRequires a certified appraisal
Hearing officerValue or uniformityReal property that is not a homestead and is valued above $500,000, plus large personal property accounts
Superior CourtAs agreedOnly by written agreement with the assessors

Within 10 business days of a request, the assessors owe you the records behind your value, so ask early. Comparable sales and photos of defects the county could not see from the road make the usual evidence. The rate itself is off the table, since an appeal reaches value, uniformity and taxability only.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can a Clayton County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
A homestead is the one house you own and occupy as your primary residence on January 1, and nobody can hold two. Applications go to the Tax Commissioner. The county says it takes them all year, but the filing window is January 2 to April 1 and a late one waits for the following year. After approval the exemption renews itself, and the owner's only duty is to report a loss of eligibility.

A local base-year homestead measure was prepared for Clayton voters on the November 4, 2025 ballot. As the commissioner's office described it, the measure would freeze the county-purposes value for senior residents age 65 or older, disabled veterans, surviving spouses of peace officers or firefighters killed in the line of duty, and 100 percent disabled residents, for tax years 2026 through 2030. Ask the commissioner's office whether your parcel is covered.

A homestead exemption follows the occupant. A buyer files separately after moving in, so the next bill on the house can run higher than yours did.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes go unpaid on a Clayton County house?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes lead to an execution on the property and, eventually, a tax sale. The Tax Commissioner's property portal links to tax sale notices for the October 2026 and November 2026 sales, a bidder pre-registration form, and an excess funds claim form for owners owed money after a sale. Those links show how active the process is in a county this size.

A tax sale transfers a tax deed and not clear title, and Georgia law gives the owner a right to redeem. A house with a tax lien on it is hard to finance. Lenders want the account clear, and the closing office will deduct any balance from your proceeds. If you are behind, call (770) 477-3311 first and ask what it takes to clear the account by your target closing date.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when you sell in Clayton County?
sections.html:
The county does not split the year between buyer and seller. That split lives in your sales contract and settlement statement, which the closing attorney prepares. Have the closing office request a payoff covering the county bill and any city bill.

  • Pull your current bill from the Tax Commissioner's portal and note whether a city bill also applies.
  • Ask whether an appeal is pending, because a pending appeal means a second bill for the remaining 15%.
  • Confirm any homestead exemption will be removed after the sale.
  • Keep the closing statement. It is your record that the bill was paid.

A sale with tenants or a repair list can still close on a cash timeline, so weigh any written cash offer against what a listing would net.

faqs.q: What is the filing deadline for a Clayton County value appeal?
faqs.a: The deadline is 45 days after the mailing date on your notice, and the appeal must be in writing. Take it to the assessors at 121 S. McDonough Street, Annex 3, fourth floor, in Jonesboro, or use the county's online appeals site. A late one leaves the value standing for the year.

faqs.q: Which Clayton County office answers bill questions, and which handles values?
faqs.a: Bills, payments, exemptions and payoffs go to the Tax Commissioner at (770) 477-3311. Values, notices and appeals go to the assessors at (770) 477-3285. The assessors collect nothing, and the commissioner changes no values.

faqs.q: Do I pay anything while a Clayton County appeal is pending?
faqs.a: Yes, most of it. A parcel under appeal receives two bills. The 85% bill is due on the usual date. The other 15% is settled after the decision, and that can mean a small balance or a refund.

faqs.q: Can a Clayton County house with unpaid taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes come out of your proceeds at the closing table, so get a payoff figure for the closing date. A parcel already sold at a tax sale needs one more step, because the tax deed buyer holds an interest until redemption. Start with a call to (770) 477-3311.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption pass to the buyer of my Clayton County house?
faqs.a: No. The exemption belongs to the person who lives in the home. A buyer files a new application with the Tax Commissioner, and one filed after April 1 is processed for the following year.
